title: Serve canonical versioned owned pages through existing GREG console
problem: The machine can produce assets but cannot yet serve canonical versioned owned pages; successful component proofs must continue into an integrated private serving path.
baseline: Guarded Foundry, media, portable community, journeys and actual packaging at PR147; serving is founder console only.

alternatives.name: simplest_viable_alternative
alternatives.description: Reuse GREG console, ArtifactStore, #3 versions and guarded query for private receipt-bound owned pages.
advantages: Integrates actual HTTP serving without another server or authority.
disadvantages: Public deployment and customer portal operations remain unfinished.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Demanded public deployment/portal functions and available authorized host.

alternatives.name: strongest_competing_architecture
alternatives.description: Owned Discourse/Ghost/FastAPI instance behind a separately governed deployment.
disadvantages: No owned instance or deployment authority is connected; duplicating the founder console would drift.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Authorized deployment target, operational requirements and verified authority integration.

alternatives.name: reversible_experiment
alternatives.description: Actual loopback HTTP serving of a signed GREG mission, hostile Host refusal, unsigned-file exclusion and corruption refusal in CI.
advantages: Measures executable serving and receipt binding.
disadvantages: Private fixture HTTP does not prove public adoption or legal rights.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Later authorized public operation without leaving buildable private machinery unfinished.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Leave native production disconnected from the owned serving path.

roles.position: Connect production to actual owned serving, then automatically continue the full machine. One agent applying distinct perspectives, not independent reviews.
material_concerns: Filesystem presence could be mistaken for approved owned content.

roles.position: Reuse existing console, byte store and version mechanism; add no second kernel or authority. One agent applying distinct perspectives, not independent reviews.
material_concerns: Serving could create a second authority path or expose content publicly.

roles.position: Unreceipted files, corrupt bytes and hostile Host requests must be refused. One agent applying distinct perspectives, not independent reviews.
material_concerns: Edited content, version links or source declarations could break provenance.

roles.position: Keep serving read-only, bounded, version-aware and scoped to known missions. One agent applying distinct perspectives, not independent reviews.
material_concerns: Source input could execute browser code or cause path traversal.

roles.position: Private HTTP, declarations and test acceptance cannot establish public operation, rights or real demand; expose dependency/skip limits. One agent applying distinct perspectives, not independent reviews.
material_concerns: Dependency skips could conceal technically achievable solver machinery.

evidence.claim: Owned community and journey predecessor integrated
evidence.finding: All six CI jobs passed atca8465b6; full suite1578 passed/74 skipped; V1–V5 passed. This does not validate the new serving delta.

counterevidence.claim: Passing private serving establishes public deployment or machine completion
counterevidence.finding: It does not. Public deployment, authentication/collection, broader portal operations and every other unfinished machine requirement remain open.

pass_1.intended_outcome: Serve retained canonical owned content from the one existing private GREG console, then continue the parent machine objective.

advantages.amplified_value: A signed mission produces pages that the existing HTTP server can return.
Approved bytes, not arbitrary filesystem presence, enter the index.
Corrections keep previous content and provenance without parallel versioning.
Every page open independently checks immutable bytes and receipt addresses.
Existing optional solvers run in full-suite CI instead of silently skipping feasible mechanisms.

disadvantages.statement: Filesystem presence could be mistaken for approved owned content.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Serve only versions named in successful canonical foundry.apply receipts, with witness/grant-dispatch and mission binding; unsigned files never enter the index.

disadvantages.statement: Serving could create a second authority path or expose content publicly.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Reuse the existing console and its loopback/Host protections. Production still crosses GREG Authority Office/Gate; add no public bind or activation.

disadvantages.statement: Edited content, version links or source declarations could break provenance.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Re-read guarded staged stores, verify immutable addresses and version chain, and compare served page/version addresses with the retained receipt.

disadvantages.statement: Source input could execute browser code or cause path traversal.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Render bounded canon as escaped text; reject invalid object names and scope reads to known mission workspaces. Preserve Host/CSP controls.

disadvantages.statement: Dependency skips could conceal technically achievable solver machinery.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Install existing cognition requirements in the complete-suite CI job, record optional runtime dependency versions in the build manifest, and keep actual skip counts explicit.
